voice_text: Have you ever wondered how a tiny seed grows into a huge tree? Animals eat food to get energy, but plants do not eat. Plants make their own food, and they do it using sunlight. This wonderful process is called photosynthesis, and in this lesson we will learn how it works.

voice_text: Living things that make their own food are called autotrophs. Green plants are autotrophs. Animals and humans cannot make their own food, so they depend on plants and other animals. That is why they are called heterotrophs. Almost all the food we eat comes, directly or indirectly, from plants that make food by photosynthesis.

visual_instruction: Two groups: plants make food (autotrophs), animals and humans eat (heterotrophs)

voice_text: Photosynthesis happens mostly in the leaves. If you look at a leaf closely, you will see tiny openings called stomata. Through the stomata, air enters and leaves the leaf. Inside the leaf cells there are small green parts called chloroplasts. These contain a green pigment called chlorophyll, which gives leaves their green colour.

voice_text: Chlorophyll is very important. It captures the energy of sunlight. Without chlorophyll, a leaf cannot use sunlight to make food. This is why photosynthesis takes place only in the green parts of a plant, and not in the roots, which are not green. Some plants have red or purple leaves, but they also contain chlorophyll, hidden by other colours.

voice_text: To make food, a plant needs three raw materials. The first is sunlight, which provides energy. The second is water, which the roots absorb from the soil and send up to the leaves through tiny tubes. The third is carbon dioxide, a gas from the air, which enters the leaf through the stomata.

voice_text: Inside the chloroplasts, chlorophyll captures the energy of sunlight. This energy is used to change water and carbon dioxide into a sugar called glucose. At the same time, oxygen is released. We can write it like this: carbon dioxide plus water, in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll, gives glucose plus oxygen.

voice_text: The plant makes two products. The first is glucose, a type of sugar, which gives the plant energy to grow. The extra glucose is stored as starch, in places like potatoes and rice grains. The second product is oxygen. It leaves the leaf through the stomata and goes into the air. We and other animals breathe this oxygen.

voice_text: We can show that a leaf has made starch with a simple test. Boil the leaf in alcohol to remove its green colour, then pour a few drops of iodine solution on it. If starch is present, the leaf turns blue black. A leaf kept in the dark does not turn blue black, because without light it could not make starch.

voice_text: Photosynthesis is important for all life on Earth. It gives food to plants, and through plants to animals and humans. It also keeps the air balanced, because plants take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen. Forests and green spaces help keep our air fresh. That is why we should protect plants and plant more trees.

voice_text: Let us remember. Plants make their own food by photosynthesis. It happens in the green leaves, using chlorophyll. The raw materials are sunlight, water and carbon dioxide. The products are glucose and oxygen. Extra glucose is stored as starch. Now think: what would happen to life on Earth if plants stopped making food?
